title: Arras for Godot 4 is live: your playthrough, woven into a tapestry
html:
Arras is live for Godot 4. It turns what a player did into a Bayeux style embroidered hanging they can open and scroll: one woven panel per act, with figures, a border, a ground and a stitched Latin inscription that names the act in your own words. 48 scenes, 16 figures, 12 props, 10 border registers, 5 grounds and 6 dye sets, and every figure, letter and stitch is drawn at runtime by code. No image file ships.

What it does

  • The words choose the scene. chronicle.weave("The oath at Roven") weaves an oath; "Crossing the narrow sea" weaves a voyage. Words match whole words, so "burn" matches "burned" but never a name like "Burnley". Name the scene yourself if you prefer.
  • Every act is frozen when it is woven (scene, border, ground, seed), so an update can never re weave a hanging a player has already saved.
  • A scrolling hanging on a carved rod with a fringed hem, its borders running on from panel to panel. Only the panels near the view are stitched.
  • PNG export of one panel or the whole hanging, for an ending screen your players can share.

How it is drawn

Every outline is a stem stitch, short laps slanted against the line and tinted by how each faces the light. Every fill is laid and couched work, a flat wool with a fine grain and a lattice of tacks. The linen weave runs through faces and hands. A panel takes about 20 to 50 ms to stitch on the test machine, once; after that scrolling a 40-act hanging end to end measured a median frame of under 3 ms with vsync off, on both renderers.

Tested

  • Every scene photographed under Forward+ and Compatibility: 96 frames, zero engine errors, all 48 measured as distinct pictures against a bare panel.
  • The shipped zip installed into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project under both renderers: three routes to a panel, a chronicle in a hanging, PNG export, save and load, every scene reading its own sample title, all six dye sets.
  • 7 attacks, including odd paths, a 40 act hanging scrolled end to end, a third renderer and bad inputs; 115 Readme claims checked against the shipped files.

Free lite

The page carries a free MIT lite: twelve of the scenes with the same panel, hanging, chronicle and demo.

Where this line stands: 17 Godot packs live from this studio, 0 purchases so far (read from the store the day this went live).

Disclosure: the scripts, shader, Latin formulae and sample titles were written with AI. The cover was rendered by the pack itself.
